importance_ranking.reason: Glass cabin sub-types (full glass, half-glass/half-solid, frameless, framed, portable standalone) are visually distinct and non-interchangeable for a given project brief. Buyers scan images first to identify cabin style; wrong visual type causes an immediate skip before any text is read.

Frame material (aluminium vs MS), glass thickness, and design type (framed/frameless) are primary shortlisting criteria that determine structural suitability and compliance with IS 2553. Without these specs, a contractor cannot evaluate whether the product meets project requirements.

Per-sq-ft rate varies substantially with glass thickness, frame material, and glazing style — buyers compare rates only after spec equivalence is confirmed. Indian fit-out contractors are price-aggressive and actively compare across multiple vendors; price is a decisive shortlisting lever once spec matches.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Dominant unit for office cabin partitioning work. Standalone portable cabins and guard booths are quoted per piece — listings for these sub-types must show unit explicitly to prevent price comparison confusion with per-sq-ft office cabin listings.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece is a genuine market ambiguity between office partition cabins and standalone portable cabins. Price cannot be meaningfully compared without knowing the unit; omitting it causes buyer confusion and misquotation risk.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Saint-Gobain is actively cited by buyers and sellers as a glass brand signal in the Indian office cabin market; buyers specify Saint-Gobain glass as a quality proxy in project briefs.
importance_ranking.reason: Seller's fabrication and installation capability, track record, and glass brand sourcing (Saint-Gobain) are evaluated after price shortlisting — particularly by institutional buyers (banks, IT companies) who need post-sale installation assurance.
